{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java",
      "line": 73,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId",
      "body": "AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId can therefore be stored and later encoded as the literal string 'null' or produce an invalid token ID. The check should validate rawTokenId, and ideally reject empty values as well."
    },
    {
      "file": "testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java",
      "line": 483,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "isAccessTokenId matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut",
      "body": "AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals the expected grant shortcut. The grant shortcut is at zero-based positions 4 and 5, i.e. substring(4, 6), and the condition should reject mismatches. As written, the matcher checks the wrong two characters and inverts the test, so it does not verify the grant shortcut at all. It also calls substring without checking that the prefix is at least six characters, which can throw for malformed IDs."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java",
      "line": 74,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Grant shortcuts are not validated for format or null values",
      "body": "DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit reads OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() and stores it directly in maps. The encoder/decoder assumes every shortcut is exactly two characters, because the token prefix must be six characters total, but there is no validation that shortcuts are non-null, non-empty, exactly two characters, or safely unique. A custom grant factory returning a three-character shortcut, which is encouraged by the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory Javadoc saying '3-letters', will produce token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId later rejects. A null shortcut will cause a NullPointerException."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 33,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "New getShortcut method is a backward-incompatible SPI change",
      "body": "OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing provider-factory interface, and this PR adds an abstract String getShortcut() method without a default implementation. Existing implementations outside this repository will fail to compile and already-compiled implementations can fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when Keycloak invokes the new method. If this interface is intended to be implemented by extensions, this should be introduced in a compatible way, for example with a default method or explicit migration guidance."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java",
      "line": 113,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Lazy shortcut map updates bypass duplicate validation and can overwrite mappings",
      "body": "getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily insert entries into grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts when an unknown grant or shortcut is encountered. These lazy updates do not re-run the startup validation for duplicate shortcuts or IDs, so a dynamically available grant with a colliding shortcut can silently overwrite an existing mapping and cause incorrect grant-type resolution. The two maps are also updated separately, so they can be observed in a temporarily inconsistent state."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null or malformed IDs safely",
      "body": "DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId immediately calls encodedTokenId.indexOf(':') without checking for null, so a null token ID causes a NullPointerException. It also accepts inputs such as 'onrtac:' and creates a context with an empty raw token ID, because AccessTokenContext does not properly validate rawTokenId. If this method is used to parse token IDs from incoming requests, malformed IDs should result in controlled validation errors rather than NPEs or invalid contexts."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId can therefore be stored and later encoded as the literal string 'null' or produce an invalid token ID. The check should validate rawTokenId, and ideally reject empty values as well.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
findings.body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals the expected grant shortcut. The grant shortcut is at zero-based positions 4 and 5, i.e. substring(4, 6), and the condition should reject mismatches. As written, the matcher checks the wrong two characters and inverts the test, so it does not verify the grant shortcut at all. It also calls substring without checking that the prefix is at least six characters, which can throw for malformed IDs.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not validated for format or null values
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit reads OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() and stores it directly in maps. The encoder/decoder assumes every shortcut is exactly two characters, because the token prefix must be six characters total, but there is no validation that shortcuts are non-null, non-empty, exactly two characters, or safely unique. A custom grant factory returning a three-character shortcut, which is encouraged by the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory Javadoc saying '3-letters', will produce token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId later rejects. A null shortcut will cause a NullPointerException.

findings.title: New getShortcut method is a backward-incompatible SPI change
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing provider-factory interface, and this PR adds an abstract String getShortcut() method without a default implementation. Existing implementations outside this repository will fail to compile and already-compiled implementations can fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when Keycloak invokes the new method. If this interface is intended to be implemented by extensions, this should be introduced in a compatible way, for example with a default method or explicit migration guidance.

findings.title: Lazy shortcut map updates bypass duplicate validation and can overwrite mappings
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily insert entries into grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts when an unknown grant or shortcut is encountered. These lazy updates do not re-run the startup validation for duplicate shortcuts or IDs, so a dynamically available grant with a colliding shortcut can silently overwrite an existing mapping and cause incorrect grant-type resolution. The two maps are also updated separately, so they can be observed in a temporarily inconsistent state.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null or malformed IDs safely
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId immediately calls encodedTokenId.indexOf(':') without checking for null, so a null token ID causes a NullPointerException. It also accepts inputs such as 'onrtac:' and creates a context with an empty raw token ID, because AccessTokenContext does not properly validate rawTokenId. If this method is used to parse token IDs from incoming requests, malformed IDs should result in controlled validation errors rather than NPEs or invalid contexts.
